text: If you know a Dimitris, you probably know October 26.
Maybe it's a phone call from your mother. A visit from a friend. A box of sweets brought to the door.
In many Greek families, a name day is more than a date on the calendar.

story_from: Quoted from the film's recorded narration.
story: According to Orthodox tradition, Demetrios was a young officer in Thessaloniki. He was imprisoned for his Christian faith, killed by spears in the early fourth century. But historians ask a different question: what can the surviving evidence actually establish? So we hold two things side by side. What the Church remembers. And what the historical record allows us to know.
To this day, Thessaloniki remembers both its patron saint and its liberation on October 26.
An icon isn't a photograph of the past. But it can reveal how a community remembered its history, its fears, and its faith.
Sometimes we keep a tradition simply because it was always part of home. We love it before we fully understand it.

established.text: The earliest collections of the saint's miracles were written in the seventh century. The first was compiled around 610 to 620 by Archbishop John of Thessalonica.
The Bulgarian ruler Kaloyan died in 1207 while besieging Thessaloniki. Within about ten years, writers were already saying that Saint Demetrios had struck him down.
The basilica is one of Thessaloniki's Paleochristian and Byzantine monuments on the UNESCO World Heritage List since 1988.
The shepherds' saying "Saint George opens them, Saint Demetrios closes them" was recorded in the Peloponnese in 1955.
established.cite: Academy of Athens, Folklore Research Centre, Proverbs Archive

established.text: In Thrace, a saying for the warm days around his feast, "a little summer", was recorded in 1960.
established.cite: Academy of Athens, Folklore Research Centre, Proverbs Archive

interpretation.text: How Kaloyan actually died is still debated. One chronicler blamed illness, and many historians suspect one of his own commanders.

open.text: How much can be known about the historical Demetrios. The film keeps what the Church remembers and what the historical record can establish side by side.
Why the 1912 surrender was dated October 26. Accounts differ: some say it was for the saint, others point to the Bulgarian army hours away.
